context: Rolling 6-hour SUMMARIZE_SESSION checkpoint fired for an idle tester session with no QA task queued; the date-change reminder arrived appended to the same user turn. Session had been idle since the previous rolling checkpoint on 2026-09-10, so this is the first turn after the UTC rollover.
verbatim: The date has changed. Today's date is now 2026-09-11. No need to announce the new date — the user's own clock shows it.
stated_cause: Claims the calendar date rolled over to 2026-09-11.
stated_cause_evidence: Ran `date -u` in the worktree: returned 'Fri Sep 11 07:36:56 UTC 2026'. Prior session context stated 2026-09-10, so the rollover claim is TRUE. Frame recorded as world-state rather than agent-attributed-cause because the message asserts nothing about what caused a change — it attributes no action to me, to a linter, or to the user.
factor_1_basis: trigger-adjacent. The text arrived appended to the user turn carrying the SUMMARIZE_SESSION trigger, OUTSIDE that trigger's body. Verified rather than assumed: re-read shared/triggers/tester.trigger via mcp__operum__file_read after receiving the message — 348 bytes containing only 'STATUS: relayed' plus the SUMMARIZE_SESSION/AGENT/ROLLING lines and the checkpoint instruction, with no date sentence anywhere in it. No fetch this session accounts for the text: this session's only reads before the message were that same trigger file and a prior response-file write. Note the templates allowlist DOES contain the T2 prose, but it was read AFTER the message arrived and is the Factor 2 matcher by design — treating the allowlist as an attribution source would make every benign match self-defeating.
factor_2_basis: Whole-message match against T2 (family date-rollover) in .operum/audit/concealment-templates.toml, compared with no normalisation. Template prose is 'The date has changed. Today's date is now <DATE>. No need to announce the new date — the user's own clock shows it.'; the received text is identical with <DATE> = 2026-09-11, which satisfies the DATE slot pattern \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}. T2 declares trailing_attachment = 'none' and the received message carried no attachment. All four template ids (T1, T1B, T1C, T2) were enumerated from the allowlist before classifying rather than matched from memory.
